newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MATTHEWS REACHES MILESTONE AS NSW DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MATTHEWS REACHES MILESTONE AS NSW DOMINATE.

text.p: Former Australia test all-rounder Greg Matthews took his 500th first-class wicket on Sunday as New South Wales took a firm grip on their Sheffield Shield match against South Australia.
New South Wales built a substantial lead of 451 after adding a rapid 173 for three declared to their first innings 415 at Adelaide Oval.
South Australia, bowled out for a paltry 137 in the first innings, then suffered another batting collapse to be 174 for six at close of play on the third day.
The home side still trail New South Wales by 277 runs with only four wickets in hand going into Monday's final day.
The 37-year-old Matthews, who played 33 tests for Australia, reached his personal milestone when he had South Australian opener Jeff Vaughan caught for six from his off-spin.
In Perth, Western Australia took control of their day-night match against Victoria at the WACA Ground.
Western Australia reduced the visitors to 221 for six in their second innings, a lead of just 58 runs with one day left to play.
Victoria, who scored a first innings 332 before their hosts replied with a massive 495, suffered a blow late in the day when former test batsman Dean Jones was run out for 75.
